questions.question: P(A | B) is read as...
options: The probability of A and B
The probability of A given that B has occurred
The probability of B given A
questions.explanation: The vertical bar means 'given'. P(A | B) is the probability of A inside the smaller world where B is known to have happened.

questions.question: In a probability tree, how do you find the probability of a whole path?
options: Multiply the branch probabilities along the path
questions.explanation: Multiply along a path to get the joint probability of that sequence. Add across paths when several paths lead to the same event.

questions.question: Of 100 students who studied, 90 passed. Of 100 who didn't study, 40 passed. What is P(pass | studied)?
questions.explanation: Restrict to the 100 who studied: 90/100 = 0.90. (0.65 is the overall pass rate, and 0.692 is P(studied | pass).)

questions.question: In the same data, 90 of the 130 who passed had studied. What is P(studied | pass)?
questions.explanation: Restrict to the 130 who passed: 90/130 ≈ 0.692. It differs from P(pass | studied) = 0.90. P(A|B) and P(B|A) answer different questions.

questions.question: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. What is P(both red)?
questions.explanation: P(first red) = 4/10, then P(second red | first red) = 3/9. Multiply: 12/90 = 2/15 ≈ 0.133.

questions.question: In the Monty Hall puzzle (you picked door 1, the host opened a goat door 3), what is the chance of winning if you switch?
questions.explanation: Your original pick keeps its 1/3 chance. The remaining 2/3 collapses onto the one other unopened door because the host must reveal a goat. Switching wins 2 times out of 3.
